name: Vocabulary in Context
title: Vocabulary in Context
answer: Vocabulary in Context is the idea that students learn words best by meeting them many times in meaningful settings, not by memorizing definitions from a list. AI tools help teachers build those settings quickly, through short passages that reuse the same words in different situations and through picture cards for younger students and English learners. The teacher still decides which words are worth teaching.

crumbs.name: Reading and Writing, Kindergarten Through 12th Grade

sections.body: A word becomes known to a student through repeated meetings in real contexts, not through a single definition handed over once. AI tools can produce short passages that place the same set of vocabulary words into several different situations, such as sports, science, and a family trip. Seeing a word used in different ways gives students a fuller sense of what it means and how it behaves in a sentence. The problem this solves is the thinness of vocabulary work built on lists, where students memorize a definition and never watch the word do anything. The tool widens the practice around words the teacher has already chosen, without taking over the choosing.
sections.heading: The idea

sections.body: A teacher might ask a tool for three short paragraphs that use the same five words, each paragraph set in a different context. For younger students and English learners, pictures carry much of the load, and a tool such as Canva for Education can pair each word with an image and a simple sentence. The teacher checks that each picture actually shows the word's meaning, since generated images can be misleading. A small set of picture cards can be reused all year and sent home for practice. The text draws its main distinction between younger students and English learners on one side and older students working with passages on the other, rather than naming separate grade bands.
sections.heading: How it works in school

sections.body: The text supplies no study, figure, or evidence label for this idea. It states as a working principle that students learn words best when they meet them in meaningful context, many times over, and it does not attach a citation to that claim. This idea therefore rests on practice rather than research as the book presents it.
sections.heading: What the evidence says

sections.body: The teacher remains the judge of which words matter. AI tools will happily generate long lists, but students learn most from a few important words taught deeply. Teachers should choose words that unlock the texts students will read and the subjects they will study. The tool's job is to make practice with those words richer, not to decide what to teach. The teacher also holds the check on generated images, because a picture that does not show the word's meaning teaches the wrong thing.
